text:
olivia: Heads-up — us-west1-b GPUs at ~95% for the last 30m. Pending pods piling up, some >2m. Thinking we need a fanout to warm pools in us-west1-a + a regional burst policy. Anyone oncall?

sam-ops: Looking now. Are these spot/preemptible nodepools or on-demand? Which pool name?

olivia: Mostly spot. nodepool = `gpu-spot-b`. autoscaler shows "could not find available machine" errors. Example from pending pods: `ImagePullBackOff` not the issue; it's `0/12 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient accelerators`.

cheng: If CA can't provision in-zone, we should have a clear fallback ladder: same-zone -> region-warm -> region-on-demand -> cross-region as last resort. Region-warm would be tainted nodes ready to accept tolerations.

ira: Warm pools cost money. Quick calc: 3 T4s kept warm in a region ~= $1.6k/mo. But avoids 30–90s cold spin-up which kills tail latency. We need SLO gating for cross-region burst. Don't silently ship cross-region unless SLO allows it.

leah-mlinfra: Also remember KV cache locality: cross-region fallbacks will suffer cache misses and extra model warmup. Might be better to degrade model (smaller quantized) for cross-region traffic than move heavy jobs.

auto-scaler-bot: scale_attempt: tried to create 4 GPUs in us-west1-b; failed due to quota/INSUFFICIENT_CAPACITY.

sam-ops: Proposal: create `gpu-warm-regional` nodepool with taint `dedicated=warm:NoSchedule` + toleration at router level; keep N warm nodes per region (configurable, default 2-3). Router sets header `x-fallback-level`.

cheng: Implementation notes: router should attach `fallback_level` metadata and prefer_local flag. Warm nodes annotated `r-inference/pool=warm`. Use canary rollout (5% traffic) to validate. Update cluster-autoscaler config so warm pools are treated as non-autoscaled (or low autoscale floor).

ira: We also need PodDisruptionBudget and eviction policy changes for streaming workloads — long-lived streams shouldn't be abruptly moved cross-region. Consider async enqueue + retry path for overflow.

leah-mlinfra: Test plan: synthetic load test with 500 concurrent seq=2048 requests, simulate zone outage, assert p95 latency < 750ms for critical tier and cache-warm-rate metric >= 60% after fallback. Add regression alert on increased token cost per request when falling back.

sam-ops: Quick create script snippet I'm going to run (will keep small):
```bash
gcloud container node-pools create gpu-warm-regional \
  --cluster=redwood-prod --zone=us-west1-a \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-t4,count=1 \
  --node-taints=dedicated=warm:NoSchedule --num-nodes=3
```

olivia: Nice. I'll update the runbook with fallback ladder and include cost thresholds. Also adding metric `cache_warm_rate` and `fallback_cross_region_rate`.

sam-ops: Tagging this for eng-sre sprint. @ira can you add the cost calc to the PR and @leah-mlinfra can you own the load test? :+1:

auto-scaler-bot: created nodepool `gpu-warm-regional` in us-west1-a (3 nodes) — success.

olivia: Thanks all — plan: 1) warm pool up (sam) 2) router header + toleration (cheng) 3) run canary (leah) 4) cost review (ira). I'll post updates in the runbook channel.
